tasks.title: Narrow classifyStartupFailure so RESUME_FAILED requires wording that names the session
acceptance: With a resume requested, a startup failure whose message is `Claude Code process exited with code 1. stderr: failed to resume: spawn ENOENT` (the shape the SDK builds: `getProcessExitError` message plus `formatStderrTail`'s `. stderr: <tail>`, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs) is classified `SPAWN_FAILED`, asserted by a test in tests/unit/pod/errors.test.ts. At fa113f2 the bare `resume` alternative in the regex at src/main/pod/errors.ts:63 classifies it `RESUME_FAILED`. The test is shown able to fail (test discipline, Coverage: 'A test is shown able to fail'): restoring the bare `resume` alternative at that one regex site turns it red, with the command and failure reported.

With a resume requested, a message of the same SDK shape whose stderr tail is the CLI 2.1.235 string `No conversation found with session ID: 30f2c781-82d3-404f-a84b-c551e77ae658` is classified `RESUME_FAILED`, asserted by its own test. PRESERVED behaviour (already true at fa113f2); shown able to fail by removing from the regex the alternative that accepts this wording.

With a resume requested, a message of the same SDK shape whose stderr tail is the CLI 2.1.235 string `Session not found in any project directory` is classified `RESUME_FAILED`, asserted by its own test. PRESERVED behaviour (already true at fa113f2); shown able to fail by removing from the regex the alternative that accepts this wording.

With a resume requested, a message of the same SDK shape whose stderr tail is the CLI 2.1.235 string `Error: Invalid session ID. Must be a valid UUID.` is classified `RESUME_FAILED`, asserted by its own test. PRESERVED behaviour (already true at fa113f2); shown able to fail by removing from the regex the alternative that accepts this wording.

With a resume requested, a message of the same SDK shape whose stderr tail is the CLI 2.1.235 string `Invalid session_id: contains unsafe characters` is classified `RESUME_FAILED`, asserted by its own test. PRESERVED behaviour (already true at fa113f2); shown able to fail by removing from the regex the alternative that accepts this wording.

With a resume requested, a message of the same SDK shape whose stderr tail is `session started; working directory not found` (the word `session` and the phrase `not found` in unrelated clauses) is classified `SPAWN_FAILED`, asserted by a test. At fa113f2 the unbounded `session .*not found` alternative at src/main/pod/errors.ts:63 classifies it `RESUME_FAILED`. Shown able to fail against that unbounded alternative, with the command and failure reported.

The existing tests at tests/unit/pod/errors.test.ts:87-96 (`No conversation found to resume` with a resume id -> `RESUME_FAILED`) and :98-105 (the same message on a fresh Pod -> `SPAWN_FAILED`) remain with their messages and expected codes unchanged and pass. PRESERVED behaviour.

The docblock of `classifyStartupFailure` (src/main/pod/errors.ts:52-59 at fa113f2) no longer describes the match as broad, and states that `RESUME_FAILED` requires both a requested resume and CLI wording that names the session, which is what the caller's docblock at src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts:671-673 already states. At fa113f2 it reads 'the match is deliberately broad'.

`classifyStartupFailure`'s exported signature `(err: unknown, resumeRequested: boolean): PodRunnerError` is unchanged, so its three call sites in src/main/pod/pod-runner.ts (:200, :210, :285 at fa113f2) compile untouched. PRESERVED behaviour.

tasks.title: Clear the abandoned ccSessionId before the fresh retry in #startFreshAfterRejectedResume
acceptance: After `openPod` on a Pod stored with `ccSessionId: 'cc-gone'` whose first start rejects with `RESUME_FAILED` and whose retry comes up, and before any `onSessionId` is delivered, the stored Pod's `ccSessionId` (read through the harness's raw store) is `null`, asserted by a test in tests/unit/pod-manager/resume.test.ts. At fa113f2 it is still `'cc-gone'`, because `#startFreshAfterRejectedResume` (src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts:713-732) never writes it. Shown red against the unfixed code (red step or injected defect), with the command and failure reported (test discipline, Coverage: 'A bug fix arrives with the test that reproduces it').

In that same state (fallback done, no `onSessionId` yet), `closePod` then `openPod` builds a runner whose `options.resume` is `undefined`, asserted by a test. At fa113f2 `#start(pod, true)` reads the stored `'cc-gone'` (pod-manager.ts:598) and sends it. Shown red against the unfixed code.

In that same close-and-reopen scenario, driven by a runner double that rejects any start carrying `resume: 'cc-gone'` with `RESUME_FAILED` and accepts a start with no `resume` (modelling the CLI refusing the same id again), the Pod's count of `resume_fallback` notices is exactly 1 after the reopen and the reopened Pod's status is `idle`, asserted by a test. At fa113f2 the reopen re-sends `'cc-gone'`, is rejected, falls back again, and the count is 2. Shown red against the unfixed code. (A double that fails regardless of `resume` cannot make this observation, because it fails the fixed code's resume-less start too.)

In that same state (fallback done, no `onSessionId` yet), `reconnectPod` builds a runner whose `options.resume` is `undefined`, asserted by a test. At fa113f2 `reconnectPod` (pod-manager.ts:479-484) re-reads the store and sends `'cc-gone'`. Shown red against the unfixed code.

After `openPod` on a Pod stored with `ccSessionId: 'cc-gone'` whose first start rejects with `RESUME_FAILED` and whose retry ALSO fails (the scenario of resume.test.ts:228-242), the stored Pod is `beached` and its `ccSessionId` is `null`, asserted by a test. At fa113f2 it is `'cc-gone'`. Shown red against the unfixed code.

After that failed retry, a `reconnectPod` on the beached Pod builds a runner whose `options.resume` is `undefined` (a null id starts fresh, `#start`'s guard at pod-manager.ts:598), asserted by a test. At fa113f2 it sends `'cc-gone'`. Shown red against the unfixed code.

The clear happens BEFORE the retry starts, per the orchestrator's resolved decision for this session (unknown 2: clear before `#start(pod, false)`): at the moment the retry runner's `start()` is invoked, the stored Pod's `ccSessionId` is already `null`, asserted by a test that reads the store from inside that `start()` call. An implementation that clears only after a successful retry fails this and the failed-retry criterion above. Shown red against the unfixed code.

The `resume_fallback` notice still records the rejected id: its `abandonedCcSessionId` is `'cc-gone'` (resume.test.ts:158 at fa113f2), and that existing assertion passes unmodified. PRESERVED behaviour.

After the fresh run's `onSessionId('cc-new')`, a close and reopen resumes `'cc-new'` with the notice count still 1 (resume.test.ts:161-181 at fa113f2), and that existing test passes unmodified. PRESERVED behaviour.

The docblock of `#startFreshAfterRejectedResume` (pod-manager.ts:697-712 at fa113f2) states that the stored `ccSessionId` is cleared before the retry, why (a reopen in the window must not re-send a rejected id, and a retry that fails must not leave one on a beached Pod), and that the rejected id survives only as the notice's `abandonedCcSessionId`. At fa113f2 it says nothing about the stored id.

The docblock at pod-manager.ts:668-677 and the guard at :678 still state and implement the narrow test: `RESUME_FAILED` is acted on only when a resume id was supplied and the CLI's wording names the session; neither half is widened. PRESERVED behaviour (agreement with T1's narrowed regex and docblock is what T1's docblock criterion establishes from the other side).

The `ccSessionId` doc comment at src/shared/contracts/events.ts:199 (at fa113f2: `null before first turn`) states that the id is null both before the Pod's first turn and after the CLI rejected a resume of it (until the fresh session's first id arrives). Comment-only: `git diff fa113f2 -- src/shared/contracts/events.ts` changes no non-comment token. (Gate 2 decision.)

The `'no-session'` description at src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts:188-189 (at fa113f2: `the Pod never reached its first turn, so there is nothing on disk`) also names the rejected-resume case. Comment-only: `git diff fa113f2 -- src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts` changes no non-comment token. (Gate 2 decision.)

The comment at src/main/pod-session/remover.ts:55-56 (at fa113f2: `Null before the Pod's first turn`) also names the rejected-resume case. Comment-only: `git diff fa113f2 -- src/main/pod-session/remover.ts` changes no non-comment token. (Gate 2 decision.)

The comment at src/renderer/src/pods/DeletePodDialog.tsx:98-99 (at fa113f2: `ccSessionId is null for a Pod that never reached its first turn`) also names the rejected-resume case. Comment-only: `git diff fa113f2 -- src/renderer/src/pods/DeletePodDialog.tsx` changes no non-comment token, and the renderer hygiene/wording tests that scan this file still pass. (Gate 2 decision.)
